CASE PUD 2026-000031 ENTRY NO. 106 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 08/21/2026 - PAGE 1 OF 9




           BEFORE THE CORPORATION COMMISSION OF THE STATE OF OKLAHOMA

          IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF                    )
          OKLAHOMA GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY                      ) Case No. PUD2026-000031
          FOR COMMISSION APPROVAL OF ELECTRIC                    )
          SERVICE AGREEMENTS AND PREAPPROVAL                     )
          OF CAPACITY PURCHASE AGREEMENTS                        )
          PURSUANT TO 17 O.S. § 286(C)                           )




                                            Rebuttal Testimony

                                                       of

                                          Matthew J. Schuermann

                                                on behalf of

                                    Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company




                                              August 21, 2026




         Rebuttal Testimony of Matthew J. Schuermann                                   Page 1 of 8
         Case No. PUD2026-000031
 CASE PUD 2026-000031 ENTRY NO. 106 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 08/21/2026 - PAGE 2 OF 9




                                             Matthew J. Schuermann
                                              Rebuttal Testimony

    1    Q.    Please state your name and business address.
    2    A.    My name is Matthew J. Schuermann. My business address is 321 N. Harvey, Oklahoma
    3          City, Oklahoma, 73102.
    4
    5    Q.    Are you the same Matthew J. Schuermann who filed Direct Testimony in this case on
    6          May 1, 2026?
    7    A.    Yes, I am.
    8
    9    Q.    What is the purpose of your testimony?
   10    A.    The purpose of my testimony is to respond to arguments raised in Responsive Testimony
   11          regarding the analysis and evaluation of the two Capacity Purchase Agreements (“CPAs”)
   12          that OG&E is seeking approval of in this case. Specifically, I address questions regarding
   13          the Company’s consideration of reasonable alternatives, use of prior Request for Proposal
   14          (“RFP”) information as a market benchmark, and the importance of evaluating all available
   15          resource opportunities to secure the lowest-cost and best-value resources for customers.
   16
   17    Q.    What does Public Utility Division (“PUD”) witness Givens testify regarding the
   18          CPAs?
   19    A.    Mr. Givens recognizes that the Company has demonstrated a need for the CPA resources
   20          and acknowledges that the pricing of the CPAs compares favorably to capacity resources
   21          evaluated in the Company’s 2024 All Source RFP. However, he expresses concern that
   22          the resources were not submitted as bids through an RFP and therefore were compared
   23          against bids from a prior solicitation rather than evaluated through an ongoing competitive
   24          bidding process.1 Mr. Givens goes on to question whether reasonable alternatives were
   25          considered at all, and urges the Commission to find “that evaluation of reasonable
   26          alternatives was impossible…”2 Later Mr. Givens recommends the Commission only grant
   27          preapproval if they find it was impossible to evaluate reasonable alternatives, to set “an


         1
               Givens Responsive, 16:6–10.
         2
               Id. at 16:13–15.

         Rebuttal Testimony of Matthew J. Schuermann                                          Page 2 of 8
         Case No. PUD2026-000031
 CASE PUD 2026-000031 ENTRY NO. 106 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 08/21/2026 - PAGE 3 OF 9




    1          intentionally high bar to discourage utilities from evading RFP requirements and instead
    2          comparing resources to old, possibly outdated bids.”3
    3
    4                                             RFP PROCESS
    5    Q.    Do you agree with PUD witness Givens that the RFP OG&E used as a comparison
    6          could be considered old or outdated and cannot be relied upon by OG&E?
    7    A.    No. The comparison was made using the Company’s 2024 All Source RFP, which was the
    8          most recently completed comprehensive resource solicitation available to provide a market
    9          benchmark. The CPA pricing was in negotiation less than one year from when bids were
   10          received from the 2024 All Source RFP. OG&E witness Shoop discusses how the pre-
   11          approval statute is clear in allowing offers to be compared to bids received from an RFP
   12          within 12 months. At the time the pricing was negotiated, OG&E could rely on the pricing
   13          from the 2024 All Source RFP as a benchmark. In addition, the Company is currently
   14          conducting subsequent procurements and has visibility into more recent market offerings
   15          through those efforts. As discussed by Mr. Mossburg, prices observed in OG&E’s 2026
   16          RFPs have not declined from those prices seen in the 2024 All Source RFP.4 As a result,
   17          the 2024 All Source RFP results remain a relevant benchmark and are further supported by
   18          current market information and have been properly relied upon by OG&E to demonstrate
   19          its evaluation of the CPAs to reasonable alternatives.
   20
   21    Q.    Do you agree with PUD witness Givens that the Commission should set “an
   22          intentionally high bar to discourage utilities from evading RFP requirements…”?
   23    A.    No. There is no basis for this recommendation. First, I disagree with the insinuation that
   24          OG&E may try to “evade RFP requirements.” OG&E is very supportive of the RFP
   25          process and will continue to utilize it. However, as I explain below, sometimes there are
   26          opportunities that arise outside of an RFP process that are the best options for customers,
   27          as evidenced in this case. OG&E is not “evading RFP requirements” when it identifies
   28          resources outside of an RFP.




         3
               Id. at 18:10–14.
         4
               Mossburg Responsive, 14:12–15:2.

         Rebuttal Testimony of Matthew J. Schuermann                                          Page 3 of 8
         Case No. PUD2026-000031
 CASE PUD 2026-000031 ENTRY NO. 106 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 08/21/2026 - PAGE 4 OF 9




    1    Q.    Based on your experience, do all resource acquisition opportunities arise through a
    2          formal RFP process?
    3    A.    No. While the RFP process is an important and valuable tool that OG&E strongly supports,
    4          resource opportunities may arise outside a formal solicitation. Resource opportunities
    5          become known to the Company through a variety of channels, including bilateral
    6          discussions with developers, interactions with customers, market outreach, industry
    7          conferences, existing commercial relationships, unsolicited proposals, and ongoing
    8          procurement activities. In this case, the opportunity to secure this capacity arose during
    9          negotiations associated with Google’s electric service requirements.
   10
   11    Q.    What is OG&E’s responsibility in those situations?
   12    A.    OG&E’s obligation is to develop the lowest reasonable cost portfolio that reliably serves
   13          customers. To accomplish that objective, the Company should consider all credible
   14          resource options available to it. Limiting evaluation only to resources received through a
   15          particular solicitation could cause the Company to overlook or miss opportunities that
   16          provide significant value to customers, such as the CPAs in this case. Resource planning
   17          requires consideration of all available resources regardless of how they come to the
   18          Company’s attention. It would be irresponsible and imprudent for OG&E to ignore
   19          potentially favorable opportunities simply because they originated outside of a formal
   20          solicitation.
   21
   22    Q.    What would have happened if OGE did not contract for these CPAs and waited for a
   23          future RFP?
   24    A.    The Company would likely have lost access to this opportunity. These CPAs were offered
   25          as part of the broader commercial arrangement associated with Google’s facilities and are
   26          contingent upon the related agreements. As Mr. Mossburg observed, these resources
   27          appear to be a unique opportunity that likely would not be available in a future RFP. In
   28          addition, since execution of these agreements, the Company has continued to evaluate
   29          market alternatives through more recent procurement efforts. OG&E did not receive
   30          comparable offers for these early delivery years in either the ongoing Bridge Capacity RFP



         Rebuttal Testimony of Matthew J. Schuermann                                         Page 4 of 8
         Case No. PUD2026-000031
 CASE PUD 2026-000031 ENTRY NO. 106 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 08/21/2026 - PAGE 5 OF 9




    1          or the current All Source RFP, and the costs of resources available through those
    2          solicitations have been higher than the pricing for these CPAs.
    3
    4    Q.    Do you agree with Mr. Mossburg’s summary on page 15 of his testimony?
    5    A.    Generally, yes. Mr. Mossburg concludes that the CPAs feature reasonable protections for
    6          ratepayers, are priced substantially below comparable market alternatives, and represent a
    7          unique opportunity because they are linked to the ESA transaction. I agree with those
    8          conclusions. The Company strongly supports the RFP process and has demonstrated that
    9          commitment through numerous competitive procurements. However, as discussed above,
   10          our obligation is to pursue the best outcome for customers. If a resource opportunity
   11          presented outside of an RFP provides superior value to alternatives available through
   12          competitive solicitations or otherwise meets a need for capacity or energy that could not
   13          otherwise be met on the timeframe required, the Company should evaluate and pursue that
   14          opportunity on behalf of customers.
   15
   16                      COMPARISON OF REASONABLE ALTERNATIVES
   17    Q.    Do you agree with PUD witness Givens that a comparison of reasonable alternatives
   18          was impossible in this case?
   19    A.    No. Along with OG&E witness Shoop, I explained in my Direct Testimony how OG&E
   20          did perform a comparison of reasonable alternatives, and how RFPs are not the only way
   21          to compare reasonable alternatives. Additionally, Mr. Givens’ reasoning for his assertion
   22          is a bit confusing to me. Mr. Givens states that “the pricing under the CPAs is so favorable
   23          that any possible alternatives would be facially unreasonable.”5 I agree that the pricing
   24          under these CPAs is very favorable. That is why OG&E pursued them and ultimately
   25          contracted for them. But I reject Mr. Given’s assertion that simply because the pricing was
   26          very favorable that a comparison to reasonable alternatives is impossible.




         5
               Givens Responsive, 16:15–16.

         Rebuttal Testimony of Matthew J. Schuermann                                           Page 5 of 8
         Case No. PUD2026-000031
 CASE PUD 2026-000031 ENTRY NO. 106 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 08/21/2026 - PAGE 6 OF 9




    1    Q.    Did the Company evaluate the CPA pricing against information available from other
    2          capacity procurement opportunities?
    3    A.    Yes. As explained in my Direct Testimony, OG&E compared the CPAs to other bids
    4          offered into the Company’s 2024 All Source RFP.6 In addition, OG&E compared the
    5          CPAs to other bilateral opportunities and market transactions that were available.
    6
    7    Q.    What did OG&E’s evaluation conclude?
    8    A.    OG&E’s evaluation concluded that the price of the CPAs, and therefore the cost to
    9          customers, was lower than any other available capacity and therefore favorable as
   10          compared to reasonable alternatives. In fact, it was 26 percent lower than the lowest cost
   11          bid initially offered into the 2024 All Source RFP, and approximately 58 percent lower
   12          than the least cost CPA, and the highest ranked project, OG&E ultimately executed through
   13          the RFP.7
   14
   15    Q.    Did OG&E consider reasonable alternatives in this case?
   16    A.    Yes. OG&E exercised reasonable business judgement in evaluating and pursuing a unique
   17          opportunity that addressed an established capacity need and compared favorably to
   18          available alternatives.
   19
   20    Q.    Did any witness in this case suggest that there might be a better capacity option for
   21          OG&E?
   22    A.    No. No witnesses in this case identified any better options for capacity than the CPAs
   23          requested for approval in this case.
   24
   25    Q.    Does your testimony address all issues raised by parties in their Responsive
   26          Testimony?
   27    A.    No. My Rebuttal Testimony is limited in scope and does not address all issues raised in
   28          this proceeding. My silence on any issue should not be construed as agreement with
   29          another party’s testimony.


         6
               Schuermann Direct, 4:9–14.
         7
               Id.
